sections.title: SOLID PRINCIPLES (Part 1)
sections.body:
### 1. **Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)**
**"A class should have only ONE reason to change"**

```
❌ Bad: UserManager (saves DB, sends emails, generates reports)
✅ Good: User, UserRepository, EmailService, ReportGenerator
```

**Examples:**
- User management system
- Data processing pipeline
- Service layer separation

### 2. **Open/Closed Principle (OCP)**
**"Open for extension, closed for modification"**

```
❌ Bad: if/elif chain for each shape type
✅ Good: Abstract Shape class, extend with Circle/Rectangle/Triangle
```

**Examples:**
- Shape area calculator
- Payment processors
- Plugin systems

### 3. **Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)**
**"Subclasses should be substitutable for their base classes"**

```
❌ Bad: Penguin(Bird) that throws exception on fly()
✅ Good: Bird → FlyingBird/SwimmingBird hierarchy
```

**Examples:**
- Bird taxonomy
- Vehicle types
- Employee hierarchies

### 4. **Interface Segregation Principle (ISP)**
**"Don't force clients to depend on methods they don't use"**

```
❌ Bad: WorkerInterface with work(), eat(), sleep()
✅ Good: Separate Workable, Eatable, Sleepable interfaces
```

**Examples:**
- Worker types (Human vs Robot)
- Device capabilities
- User permissions

### 5. **Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)**
**"Depend on abstractions, not concretions"**

```
❌ Bad: Application → MySQLDatabase (tight coupling)
✅ Good: Application → Database Interface ← MySQL/Postgres/Mongo
```

**Examples:**
- Database abstraction
- Payment gateway integration
- Notification services

diagrams.title: SOLID in one picture
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  s["S · Single responsibility: one reason to change"] --> o["O · Open/closed: extend with new classes, don’t edit old ones"]
  o --> l["L · Liskov substitution: subclasses must honour the base contract"]
  l --> i["I · Interface segregation: small, focused interfaces"]
  i --> d["D · Dependency inversion: depend on abstractions, inject concrete classes"]
  d --> goal["Code that is easy to test, change and extend"]
diagrams.explain: SOLID is five checks for class design. Split classes that change for different reasons; add behaviour by adding classes rather than editing `if/elif` chains; make sure subclasses can stand in for their parent; keep interfaces small so classes do not implement methods they cannot support; and depend on abstractions so implementations (a MySQL or a Postgres repository) can be swapped and mocked.

sections.title: CREATIONAL PATTERNS
sections.body:
### 1. **Singleton Pattern** (Part 1)
**"Ensure only ONE instance exists"**

```python
db1 = DatabaseConnection()
db2 = DatabaseConnection()
assert db1 is db2  # Same instance!
```

**Use Cases:**
- Database connections
- Configuration managers
- Logger instances
- Cache managers

### 2. **Factory Pattern** (Part 1)
**"Create objects without specifying exact class"**

```python
factory = NotificationFactory()
email = factory.create('email')
sms = factory.create('sms')
```

**Use Cases:**
- Notification systems (Email, SMS, Push)
- Payment methods (Card, PayPal, Crypto)
- Document generators (PDF, Word, Excel)

### 3. **Builder Pattern** (Part 2)
**"Construct complex objects step by step"**

```python
computer = ComputerBuilder()
    .set_cpu("Intel i9")
    .set_ram("32GB")
    .set_gpu("RTX 4090")
    .build()
```

**Use Cases:**
- Building computers with many components
- Creating complex configurations
- Pizza/meal ordering systems
- Query builders

### 4. **Prototype Pattern** (Part 2)
**"Create new objects by cloning existing ones"**

```python
warrior_template = GameCharacter("Warrior", 150, 50, 40)
warrior1 = warrior_template.clone()
warrior2 = warrior_template.clone()
```

**Use Cases:**
- Game character creation
- Document templates
- Database record duplication
- Configuration presets

### 5. **Abstract Factory Pattern** (Part 2)
**"Create families of related objects"**

```python
windows_factory = WindowsFactory()
mac_factory = MacFactory()

app = Application(windows_factory)  # Creates Windows UI
app = Application(mac_factory)      # Creates Mac UI
```

**Use Cases:**
- Cross-platform UI components
- Database drivers (MySQL, Postgres, MongoDB)
- Theme systems (Light/Dark mode)

diagrams.title: Which design pattern solves which problem
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  c["Creational — how objects are made"] --> c1["Singleton · Factory · Abstract Factory · Builder · Prototype"]
  s["Structural — how objects are composed"] --> s1["Adapter · Decorator · Facade · Proxy"]
  b["Behavioral — how objects communicate"] --> b1["Observer · Strategy · Command · Chain of Responsibility · State · Template · Iterator"]
diagrams.explain: Patterns fall into three families. **Creational** patterns control object creation (one shared instance, step-by-step construction, families of related objects). **Structural** patterns wrap or combine objects (adapt an old interface, add behaviour, simplify a subsystem, control access). **Behavioral** patterns organise communication (notify subscribers, swap algorithms, queue actions, pass requests along a chain).

sections.title: STRUCTURAL PATTERNS
sections.body:
### 6. **Adapter Pattern** (Part 2)
**"Make incompatible interfaces work together"**

```python
old_system = OldPaymentSystem()
adapter = PaymentAdapter(old_system)
# Now old_system works with new interface!
```

**Use Cases:**
- Legacy system integration
- Third-party library adaptation
- Media format converters
- API wrappers

### 7. **Decorator Pattern** (Part 3)
**"Add functionality dynamically"**

```python
coffee = SimpleCoffee()
coffee = Milk(coffee)
coffee = Sugar(coffee)
coffee = WhippedCream(coffee)
# Coffee with multiple add-ons!
```

**Use Cases:**
- Coffee shop ordering
- Text formatting (bold, italic, underline)
- Stream processing (compression, encryption)
- Middleware chains

### 8. **Facade Pattern** (Part 3)
**"Provide simplified interface to complex system"**

```python
# Instead of:
cpu.freeze()
memory.load(data)
hdd.read(sector)
cpu.execute()

# Use facade:
computer.start()  # Does everything!
```

**Use Cases:**
- Computer boot process
- Home theater system
- Complex library wrappers
- API simplification

### 9. **Proxy Pattern** (Part 3)
**"Control access to another object"**

```python
# Virtual Proxy - Lazy loading
image = ImageProxy("large_photo.jpg")  # Fast!
image.display()  # Now loads from disk

# Protection Proxy - Access control
account = BankAccountProxy(balance, user_role)
```

**Use Cases:**
- Lazy loading of expensive resources
- Access control and security
- Caching and memoization
- Remote object proxies

sections.title: BEHAVIORAL PATTERNS
sections.body:
### 10. **Observer Pattern** (Part 3)
**"Notify multiple objects about state changes"**

```python
subject = Subject()
subject.attach(EmailObserver())
subject.attach(SMSObserver())

subject.set_state("New event!")
# All observers notified!
```

**Use Cases:**
- Event handling systems
- Newsletter subscriptions
- Stock market monitoring
- MVC pattern (Model-View updates)

### 11. **Strategy Pattern** (Part 3)
**"Define family of interchangeable algorithms"**

```python
cart = ShoppingCart()
cart.set_payment_strategy(CreditCardStrategy())
cart.checkout()

cart.set_payment_strategy(PayPalStrategy())
cart.checkout()
```

**Use Cases:**
- Payment methods
- Sorting algorithms
- Compression strategies
- Route planning algorithms

### 12. **Command Pattern** (Part 4)
**"Encapsulate requests as objects"**

```python
remote = RemoteControl()
remote.execute(LightOnCommand(light))
remote.execute(TVOnCommand(tv))
remote.undo_last()  # Undo last command!
```

**Use Cases:**
- Undo/Redo functionality
- Remote controls
- Task queuing
- Macro recording
- Transaction systems

### 13. **Chain of Responsibility Pattern** (Part 4)
**"Pass request along chain of handlers"**

```python
level1 → level2 → level3 → manager

request = {"issue": "Server down", "priority": "high"}
level1.handle(request)  # Passes to appropriate level
```

**Use Cases:**
- Support ticket systems
- Expense approval chains
- Event bubbling (UI)
- Middleware processing
- Logging levels

### 14. **State Pattern** (Part 4)
**"Change behavior when internal state changes"**

```python
order = OrderContext()
# New → Processing → Shipped → Delivered
order.next_state()  # Transitions automatically
```

**Use Cases:**
- Order processing workflows
- Document approval (Draft → Review → Published)
- Game character states
- Connection states (Connecting → Connected → Disconnected)

### 15. **Template Method Pattern** (Part 4)
**"Define algorithm skeleton, let subclasses override steps"**

```python
class DataProcessor:
    def process(self):
        self.load()      # Override
        self.validate()  # Default
        self.transform() # Override
        self.save()      # Override
```

**Use Cases:**
- Data processing pipelines
- Testing frameworks
- Game AI behaviors
- Report generation

### 16. **Iterator Pattern** (Part 4)
**"Access elements sequentially without exposing structure"**

```python
library = BookCollection()
for book in library:  # Custom iteration
    print(book)
```

**Use Cases:**
- Custom collection traversal
- Filtered iteration
- Pagination systems
- Tree/graph traversal

sections.title: Pattern Comparison
sections.body:
### When to Use Which Pattern?

| Problem | Pattern | Why |
|---------|---------|-----|
| Need only one instance | **Singleton** | Global access point |
| Create objects without specifying class | **Factory** | Flexibility in object creation |
| Complex object construction | **Builder** | Step-by-step construction |
| Expensive object creation | **Prototype** | Clone instead of create |
| Create families of objects | **Abstract Factory** | Consistency across products |
| Incompatible interfaces | **Adapter** | Make it work together |
| Add features dynamically | **Decorator** | Flexible enhancement |
| Simplify complex system | **Facade** | Easy-to-use interface |
| Control access | **Proxy** | Lazy loading, security |
| One-to-many updates | **Observer** | Event notification |
| Interchangeable algorithms | **Strategy** | Runtime algorithm selection |
| Undo/Redo functionality | **Command** | Encapsulate actions |
| Sequential processing | **Chain of Responsibility** | Request handling |
| State-dependent behavior | **State** | Clean state transitions |
| Algorithm skeleton | **Template Method** | Reusable algorithm structure |
| Custom traversal | **Iterator** | Flexible iteration |

sections.title: Quick Reference
sections.body:
### SOLID Principles Checklist:
- ✅ Each class has one responsibility?
- ✅ Can extend without modifying?
- ✅ Subclasses substitutable?
- ✅ Interfaces not too big?
- ✅ Depend on abstractions?

### Pattern Selection Guide:

**Object Creation?**
- Same instance needed → Singleton
- Unknown type at compile time → Factory
- Complex construction → Builder
- Clone existing → Prototype
- Related families → Abstract Factory

**Structural Issues?**
- Incompatible interfaces → Adapter
- Add features → Decorator
- Simplify complexity → Facade
- Control access → Proxy

**Behavioral Needs?**
- Notify many objects → Observer
- Interchangeable algorithms → Strategy
- Undo/Redo → Command
- Sequential handlers → Chain of Responsibility
- State-based behavior → State
- Algorithm template → Template Method
- Custom iteration → Iterator

sections.title: Tips & Best Practices
sections.body:
1. **Start Simple**: Don't over-engineer. Use patterns when needed.

2. **SOLID First**: Apply SOLID principles before applying patterns.

3. **Real Problems**: Use patterns to solve real problems, not for the sake of patterns.

4. **Refactor**: Refactor to patterns when complexity grows.

5. **Team Knowledge**: Ensure team understands patterns you use.

6. **Documentation**: Document why you chose a pattern.

7. **Testing**: Patterns make code more testable.

8. **Performance**: Some patterns add overhead (Proxy, Decorator).

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.body:

- ✅ Improve communication among developers

- ✅ Speed up development

**Remember**: Patterns are tools, not rules. Use them wisely! 🚀
